Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the intro last week — procurement at Finlytics is starting to map our purchase path and we have two main questions where we need a quick recommendation from Redwood: 1) Should we buy via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace or sign a direct contract with Redwood, and 2) how does the co-sell credit / rebate flow work with each path?

A few specifics from our procurement side: we typically require a Purchase Order (PO) and net-30 terms for SaaS vendors, the finance team prefers a single vendor invoice, and we track partner credits separately for rebates. We're also evaluating whether a marketplace listing would speed approval.

Can you send a short comparison we can share with procurement (billing timing, invoice party, co-sell credit attribution, and any additional procurement paperwork needed)? We need to decide by the end of the month for our pilot.

Appreciate it —
Amanda Li

Finlytics Inc

Hi Amanda — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a concise comparison and a recommended path based on what most procurement teams want (short version below; attached is a one‑sheet we use internally). Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement — suggest 30 minutes.

High-level differences (AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace vs direct contract):
- Marketplace (standard listing): fast procurement for PO-driven buyers, marketplace is the billing party (vendor invoice flows through marketplace), typically supports credit card and marketplace invoice options depending on cloud provider. Good for pilots and speed-to-deploy.
- Marketplace (private offers / seller private offers): allows PO + negotiated unit price; buyer receives marketplace invoice, but we can structure a private offer to reflect negotiated pricing and connect co-sell crediting flows with the partner team.
- Direct contract (MSA + SOW): Redwood invoices directly, offers standard net-30 PO terms, required for custom terms, R&D credits, or when procurement insists on vendor-of-record. Better for multi-year or enterprise discounts.

Co-sell credit / rebate implications: 
- Marketplace: co-sell can be tracked via partner portals and private-offer metadata; however, marketplace invoices are typically issued by the marketplace operator (AWS/Azure/GCP), so co-sell crediting often happens off-invoice (partner rebate) or via partner portal settlement.
- Direct: easier to apply partner credits directly on Redwood invoice (we can create invoice line items or apply a credit memo).

Recommendation for Finlytics pilot (given timeline):
1) If procurement wants the fastest approval and is comfortable with marketplace invoicing: use AWS Marketplace private offer. This gives PO compatibility and keeps the buying experience in the cloud marketplace while preserving negotiated pricing.
2) If procurement requires Redwood as vendor-of-record or needs custom contract clauses (data retention, SOC2 addenda, export controls): sign a short direct MSA + PO and we invoice Redwood directly.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the expected spend and the accounting contact for PO issuance.
- I’ll open a private offer with AWS (if you want marketplace route) and loop Vanessa for partner credit handling.
- If direct route, Laura will prepare the MSA + standard redlines (we can pre-populate with the RFP items).

I'll attach a one-sheet and a sample MSA. If helpful, I can also include a mutual action plan and DocuSign link for the MSA.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik — internal note with recommended approach for Finlytics: 

Summary guidance:
- AWS Private Offer is our best compromise for PO-driven buyers who want speed plus negotiated pricing. Technically the marketplace is the billing party, but with a Private Offer we can: 1) set a negotiated unit price, 2) request the marketplace to include partner metadata in the purchase record, and 3) enable a private invoice flow that shows the partner information (note: not all marketplaces will surface partner credit IDs directly on the PDF invoice; oftentimes the partner portal / settlement report is where the partner credit is reconciled).
- If the client insists the vendor-of-record must be Redwood on the PDF invoice, then direct contracting is required. Finance teams occasionally accept marketplace accounting when the private offer includes the right purchase order and billing references, but you should confirm with Ben.

Practical steps to move fast (I recommend we offer both):
1) Open an AWS Private Offer with the pilot SKU and negotiated pricing (Vanessa can lead). This covers the Jan 26 PO ask and is quick to approve.
2) Simultaneously draft a short MSA + SOW for direct invoicing if they later request vendor-of-record. We can have the MSA ready to go so switching routes is painless.
3) For co-sell credits: Vanessa will document the partner credit process and provide the partner credit ID and marketplace settlement cadence (monthly/quarterly).

I attached our standard MSA for your reference. If legal redlines are needed, we'll triage but keep the pilot scope narrow to avoid long nego cycles.

Laura Bennett
Director, Contracts & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
